correctness.rationale: The hub contributes one isolated vertex, and the other faces choose at most one vertex of each matched pair. Sending the two types to ±e_i identifies the non-hub realization equivariantly with the cross-polytope boundary and then with S(R^n). Its fixed diagonal axis splits off, so taking the quotient of the join gives the unreduced suspension of S(W_n)/C_n. The base sphere is simply connected for n≥4. An equivariant simplicial model is the boundary of the standard (n−1)-simplex, radially centered at its barycenter; a barycentric subdivision makes simplex stabilizers act pointwise. For r^k the invariant subspace on that sphere is nonempty exactly when the coordinate permutation has d=gcd(n,k)>1 cycles: constants on the cycles give d variables and zero sum is one nonzero linear constraint. Armstrong's theorem therefore gives the quotient of C_n by the subgroup generated by those rotations. For n=p^a this subgroup is ⟨r^p⟩ (trivial for a=1), and for two distinct prime divisors p,q it contains r^p and r^q, hence the generator. Abelianization and suspension give the asserted H_2, and a suspension of the connected base is simply connected. At odd prime p≥5 the Fourier weights 1,…,(p−1)/2 are all nonzero and the free lens-space homology shifts up one degree, including the top degree p−1. For the symmetric quotient the sorted-coordinate slice of W_n is a cone linearly parametrized by the n−1 nonnegative successive differences; the unit slice is a closed (n−2)-ball, whose suspension is a closed (n−1)-ball. The independent `/workspace/branches/dabfbce1-d69f-477f-b7c1-146181404ecc/bounded_replay.py` replay enumerated friendship faces for n=4,…,8 and checked 4947 nonidentity rotations for n=4,…,100, corroborating face and stabilizer arithmetic. It did not compute quotient homology directly; the proof uses the stated topological theorems.

Armstrong's quotient theorem applies in the even real case too, but it does not specify the fixed elements for this action or the graph's geometric suspension. The nonequivariant chordal graph result alone does not determine the geometric orbit homology.

evidence: For odd n put m=(n−1)/2 and take weighted lens parameters (1,…,m,n) with final weight n. In the degree-two term of Eq. (2.16), s_1=lcm(1,…,m,n)/lcm(1,…,m)=n/gcd(n,lcm(1,…,m)). The zero H^1 and universal coefficient theorem give H_1=Z/s_1 for the lens quotient. For n=p^a this ratio is p because m contains the preceding p-power but not n; if n has two primes then every maximal prime power dividing n is at most m and the ratio is 1. value.rationale: The graph and action are natural before the homology computation: the same petal permutations give a simplicial sphere with a separate hub, yet the cyclic and symmetric geometric orbit spaces have different integral topology. The whole-order result identifies exactly when nontrivial integral torsion appears in the simply connected component, including powers of two where the action is not a complex lens-space model.
